[Management API](admin-api.html)

How long an access token, an ID Token and a refresh token issued here last, and how far out a clock may be before this service stops believing one of its own. Four of the settings under Configuration, behind a name that promises four rather than forty-nine — and a door that refuses a key it does not recognise instead of ignoring it.

Every answer is checked against the model shown here before it is sent, and no answer carries a member its model does not list. A member shown as *any JSON* is one whose shape belongs to somebody else, and says whose. `.{key}` is a key that is data, and `[]` an element of a list.

## GET /admin-api/token-lifetimes

`getTokenLifetimes`

**How long tokens issued here are good for**

The three lifetimes — access token, ID Token, refresh token — the clock skew applied wherever this service reads one of its own tokens back, and the two RFC 9700 mode refresh-token rules: the idle timeout and revocation on sign-out.

All six are ordinary configuration settings and appear in `GET /config` too; `settings` here is the same row shape, carrying each one's bounds, its source and its default. `lifetimes` beside it is just the three lifetimes and the skew, for a caller that wants the value rather than the provenance.

It also reports WHAT IS ALREADY OUT THERE, per kind, counted against the same clock the endpoints use — the skew is applied to that count, so a token this calls expired is one POST /oauth2/introspect will report inactive.

A LIFETIME IS STAMPED INTO A TOKEN WHEN IT IS SIGNED, so changing one reaches the next token and nothing already issued. To take an issued token out of circulation, revoke it under Tokens.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/token-lifetimes` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:read`.

## POST /admin-api/token-lifetimes/defaults

`resetTokenLifetimes`

**Put the six back**

Clears the runtime override on THESE SIX ONLY, so each falls back to its environment variable, the appconfig file, or `env/defaults.js` — one hour, one hour and twenty-four hours for the lifetimes, twenty-four hours idle, revocation on sign-out on, and thirty seconds of skew.

It is deliberately not `POST /config/reset-all`, which would also drop an override somebody set on an unrelated page. A test that changed only the lifetimes should call this to put the service back; one that changed more should call that one.

A setting that was not overridden is skipped rather than refused, because this means "put these six back" rather than "undo this one change" — the per-key refusal is on `POST /config/reset`, where it is the right answer.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/token-lifetimes` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

## POST /admin-api/token-lifetimes/set

`setTokenLifetimes`

**Set one or more of the six**

A RUNTIME OVERRIDE, like every other change made through this API: written down and re-applied at the next start when `persistence.appconfig` has a store under it (`persistence.realms` for a write made inside a realm), and gone on restart only with `persistence.mode=memory`; the reply's `message` says which. Nothing writes to the appconfig file in either case.

Name any of the six; the console form posts them all at once and a caller may post one. ALL-OR-NOTHING: every value is checked before any is written, so a body with one bad field changes nothing and names it.

UNLIKE `POST /config/set-many`, a property that is not one of the six is REFUSED rather than ignored. That door is for a form posting a whole section, where an unknown field is ordinary; this one is for a caller that means to set a lifetime, where a misspelt key that succeeded and changed nothing is the worst possible answer.

Every lifetime must be a whole number of THIRTY-SECOND units, between 30 and 2592000 (thirty days). The skew is 0 to 300 in the same units. The idle timeout is whole seconds, 0 turning it off, and revocation on sign-out is a boolean. Those bounds are on each setting's row in the GET, so a client can render them rather than repeat them.

The change applies to the NEXT token signed. Nothing already issued is affected: a lifetime is a claim inside a signed statement.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/token-lifetimes` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `oauth2.accessTokenTtlS` | integer |  | Access token lifetime (s) |
| `oauth2.clockSkewS` | integer |  | Token clock skew (s) |
| `oauth2.idTokenTtlS` | integer |  | ID Token lifetime (s) |
| `oauth2.refreshIdleSeconds` | integer |  | Refresh token idle timeout (s) |
| `oauth2.refreshTokenTtlS` | integer |  | Refresh token lifetime (s) |
| `oauth2.revokeRefreshOnLogout` | boolean |  | Revoke refresh tokens on sign-out |

**200**: What was applied, in `applied`, and what actually changed, in `changed`.
